Chapter 9: Navigating Influence in the Digital Age
The internet’s changed so much about how we connect, learn, and find our place in the world. These days, it’s almost effortless to stumble upon a group that shares your quirks, your passions, or even your wildest dreams.
But here’s the twist—it’s also never been easier to get swept up in cultish language online. Think about it: everywhere you look, there are hashtags, memes, catchy slogans, and echo chambers that just keep reinforcing one way of seeing things.
Imagine a teenager—maybe feeling alone during a rough year—who finds comfort in an online fandom. At first, it feels like a lifeline. There’s this unique language, inside jokes, secret nicknames, clever references… and suddenly, you feel like you belong. But after a while, things start to shift. Certain opinions just aren’t welcome. If you question the group’s heroes, you get shut down, fast. What started out as playful language now feels like a set of rules you have to follow.
And it’s not just fandoms. It happens in political movements, wellness circles, even casual hobby groups. The speed and reach of online conversations make it so easy for cultish language to catch on—and so tough for anyone who thinks differently to speak up.
Here’s something to really think about: online language can shape what we believe and how we act, way faster than most people realize. A simple hashtag can shrink a complicated issue down to a single slogan. And a viral meme? It can make an obscure idea feel totally normal.
The more you use that group’s language, the deeper in you get.
But let’s not forget—there’s a bright side here, too. The digital world actually gives us some powerful tools to push back. You can find new perspectives with just a few clicks. You can connect with people who love open, honest conversations. And you can help build communities where questions aren’t just allowed—they’re encouraged.
The secret? Stay curious. Notice when the words you’re using start to box you in. And look for spaces where honesty and real growth matter more than fitting in.
I know a group of friends who did exactly that. When they realized their favorite online hangout had gotten toxic, they started their own space. They made sure to use clear, inclusive language and welcomed every doubt and disagreement. Suddenly, people felt safer, more honest, and way more resilient.
So, here’s the key takeaway: language in the digital age is powerful. It can be used to control, but it can also set you free. The words you choose online? They matter now more than ever.
